claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a reported hierarchical heterostructure featuring multilevel chemical fluctuations.
Integrating high-throughput simulations with machine learning will enable accurate and efficient prediction of Young’s modulus for hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10.
Integrating high-throughput simulations with machine learning will enable accurate and efficient prediction of yield strength for hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10.
Integrating high-throughput simulations with machine learning will enable accurate and efficient prediction of toughness for hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10.
Conventional ab initio and related simulation methods impose substantial computational burdens.
Existing approaches have lower predictive capability for fracture properties than for the other targeted mechanical properties.
The alloy’s hierarchical structure and chemical fluctuations mediate local deformation mechanisms.
The alloy’s hierarchical structure and chemical fluctuations mediate local fracture mechanisms.
A sufficiently resolved high-throughput simulation dataset can capture the deformation and fracture effects of the hierarchical structure and chemical fluctuations.
Automated high-throughput simulation can efficiently explore a wide range of microstructural configurations.
A machine-learning model trained on the simulation dataset can use structure–property relationships to predict bulk mechanical properties.
The machine-learning model can approximate results otherwise obtained using computationally intensive first-principles or CALPHAD methods.
Including fracture-relevant features will improve the predictive resolution for toughness.
The proposed method will improve prediction accuracy by approximately 20–30% relative to existing individual simulation methods.
The proposed method will reduce computational time by approximately 5–10 times.
The method will robustly predict Young’s modulus.
The method will robustly predict yield strength.
The method will substantially narrow uncertainty in toughness predictions.
Reliability will diminish if emergent interfacial phenomena or heterogeneity length scales are not resolved by the simulations.
Extreme processing conditions that produce novel phases or substantial inhomogeneity will reduce model validity.
